title: How Far Can a PSRAM-less ESP32 Go? A TinyML Deployment Study for WiFi CSI HAR
description: Code, executed notebooks (with outputs), on-device measurement firmware, results, and trained models (sklearn .joblib, int8 .tflite, emlearn C) for a deployment-characterization study of WiFi CSI human activity recognition on the classic PSRAM-less ESP32. Covers classical learners, tiny neural networks, and five deep architectures on UT-HAR and CSI-HAR, with measured on-device latency, throughput, and memory for the tiny and deep tiers, a cross-subject generalization-gap analysis (leave-one-user-out vs random split), a per-user personalization study, per-class metrics with confusion matrices and significance tests, a learning-rate/batch-size sweep, and an on-device replay demo that classifies real CSI windows on the board.
